parameters.content:
# Certification Lapse Radar

Validates every staffer's certification on the date of each upcoming session, not today. The radar joins a Google Sheets roster and staffing map, a rules Data Table, and Google Calendar events for the configured window. Sessions that fall below their required certified headcount get a greedy minimal fix: the fewest renewals that restore coverage and the date they must land by. Slack gets one fix list, each lapsed staffer gets one renewal email.

## How it works
1. The weekly trigger loads Workflow Configuration, the single node holding every id and setting.
2. Google Sheets supplies the Roster tab (Person, Email, Certification, Expiry) and the Staffing tab (SessionCode, Person).
3. The Certification Lapse Radar Rules Data Table supplies session_type, required_cert, min_certified.
4. Google Calendar returns every event inside the lookahead window with recurring events expanded into dated instances.
5. The [CODE] token in each event title joins the event to staffing rows, and its prefix before the first hyphen picks the rule.
6. Each assigned staffer's expiry is compared to the session date, both sides reduced to date only with Luxon, so midnight timezone drift cannot flip a verdict.
7. Under covered sessions get the smallest renewal set, latest lapsed certs first, due by the session date. Unmatched events get their own warning section.
8. One Slack post carries fixes, unmatched warnings, and the covered count. One Gmail per lapsed staffer lists every affected session.

## Setup
1. Create a Google Sheet and put its id into Workflow Configuration as rosterSheetId, replacing ROSTER_SPREADSHEET_ID.
2. Add tab Roster with columns Person, Email, Certification, Expiry. One row per person per certification. Type Expiry as ISO text (YYYY-MM-DD) with the column formatted as plain text. The parser also survives serial numbers and common formats, but ISO text is the contract.
3. Add tab Staffing with columns SessionCode, Person. One row per assignment. Codes look like FA-101, the prefix before the first hyphen is the session type.
4. Review the Certification Lapse Radar Rules Data Table: session_type, required_cert (must match the Roster Certification text exactly), min_certified. Three sample rows are seeded, edit them to your programs.
5. Put the [CODE] token in every session calendar title, for example First Aid Refresher [FA-101]. No token means the event lands in the unmatched warning section.
6. Replace GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID and SLACK_CHANNEL_ID in Workflow Configuration and set lookaheadWeeks between 8 and 12.
7. Connect the Google Sheets, Google Calendar, Slack (invite the bot to the channel), and Gmail credentials, then activate.

## 1. Gather
Weekly trigger plus one config node holding every placeholder. Four reads follow: Roster tab, Staffing tab, rules Data Table, calendar window. Fetches after the roster carry executeOnce so upstream row counts never multiply API calls.

## 2. Validate on the session date
The [CODE] token joins each event to staffing and rules. Expiry versus session date is compared date only on both sides with Luxon. The fix is greedy and per session, no global optimizer.

## 3. Report
Sessions route three ways and each branch formats its own line. The merge collects fixes, unmatched warnings, and covered lines into one Slack post.

## 4. Email lapsed staffers
One Gmail per staffer per lapsed cert, deduped across sessions. The earliest affected session sets the renew by date. Sends continue on error, one bad address never kills the run.

## Two ways this radar can lie
1. Unmatched events are warned, never dropped. An event missing its [CODE] token, its staffing rows, or its rule cannot be validated. Silently skipping it would fake full coverage, so it gets its own Slack warning section.
2. Keep recurringEventHandling on expand. Validating only the recurring master checks only the first date of the series. Expansion checks every occurrence inside the window.
